newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Royal & Sun sees big general savings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Royal & Sun sees big general savings.

text.p: Royal & Sun Alliance, the newly merged UK composite insurer, expects its UK general business to contribute 110 million stg to total cost savings of 175 million stg by 1998, chief executive Richard Gamble told Reuters.
Royal & Sun has already said the cost of restructuring would be equivalent to about one year's savings and Gamble added that there were no indications at present this would be different.
Details of these costs are likely at the year end.
Gamble said it was the group's current intention to move its three telephone-marketed personal lines businesses much closer together over the course of next year.

The merged company has three such brands -- The Insurance Service, Royal Insurance Direct, and Sun Alliance Connections -- which between them have two million mainly household and motor insurance policies. Further structural details were unavailable.
Gamble said that rates were creeping up in the UK private motor insurance sector, a highly competitive market which is often seen as an indicator of wider future trends.
"We are getting some increases," he said, but added that they were very small single digit percentile gains.
"I think it's just going to continue in that direction," he said of the outlook for motor rates over the next six months.

The company earlier reported proforma interim pretax operating profits of 450 million stg, after 514 million a year ago, beating most analysts' forecasts of up to 435 million stg. Gamble added that Royal & Sun was still looking for a new chairman, but was unable to say whether this post would be filled by the end of the year.
"We have some targets. The process is going forward."
Royal & Sun is keen to expand overseas and is targeting the Far East, South America and India, where it hopes to get a licence early next year.
In the UK he did not rule out the acquisition of a life company over the longer term, but stressed the group was more concerned for now with completing the integration process.
